docs.title: Home
docs.text:
Guro is a reusable prompt and skill engineering library for AI agents, assistants, and application workflows. The instruction catalog is organized by modality so applications can use text, image, and audio instructions independently or through one unified package.

  • 252 instruction prompts

    A concrete, importable Python symbol for every supported instruction.

  • 172 text instructions

    Research, writing, finance, software engineering, analytics, governance, planning, and prompt engineering.

  • 45 image instructions

    Image generation, image analysis, and image editing workflows.

  • 35 audio instructions

    Translation, transcription, and speech workflows.

Get started Browse all prompts

    B --> C[text.py<br/>172 prompts]
    B --> D[image.py<br/>45 prompts]
    B --> E[audio.py<br/>35 prompts]
    C --> F[Research / Writing / Engineering / Data / Planning]
    D --> G[Generation / Analysis / Editing]
    E --> H[Translation / Transcription / Speech]

docs.title: Why Guro Is Structured This Way
docs.text:
The original catalog was a single large instructions.py module. Guro now uses an instructions/ package so modality-specific code can remain isolated while preserving a unified import surface. The package-level __init__.py re-exports the complete catalog and exposes names(), values(), items(), and get() for discovery and runtime lookup.

from instructions import ACADEMIC_WRITER, IMAGE_ANALYZER, VERBATIM_TRANSCRIBER
from instructions import get, names

You can also import only the modality required by an application:

from instructions import text, image, audio

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text: Guro separates prompt content, modality ownership, and public discovery. The package is intentionally simple: prompt values remain plain Python strings, while module boundaries provide organization and predictable imports.

docs.title: Lookup Flow
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant App as Application
    participant Init as instructions
    participant Mod as text/image/audio

    App->>Init: get("IMAGE_ANALYZER")
    Init->>Init: validate name in __all__
    Init->>Mod: resolve re-exported constant
    Mod-->>Init: prompt string
    Init-->>App: prompt string

docs.title: Public API Invariants
docs.text:
The documentation assumes the following invariants remain true:

  1. Every name in package-level __all__ resolves to a string constant.
  2. Every constant belongs to exactly one modality module.
  3. The union of submodule __all__ tuples equals package-level __all__.
  4. names(), values(), and items() preserve the declared public order.
  5. get() rejects undefined or non-public names with KeyError.
  6. Prompt Markdown remains data; helper functions do not modify prompt text.

Do not duplicate prompt ownership

A prompt should be exported from exactly one of text.py, image.py, or audio.py. The package-level module may re-export it, but two modality modules should never independently define the same public constant.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: Guro's instruction catalog is pure Python. Each prompt is exposed as a module-level string constant and can be passed directly to an LLM, image, transcription, or speech workflow that accepts instructional text.

docs.title: Import the Unified Catalog
docs.text:
Use the package-level namespace when an application may need instructions from more than one modality:

from instructions import ACADEMIC_WRITER
from instructions import IMAGE_ANALYZER
from instructions import VERBATIM_TRANSCRIBER

docs.title: Import a Modality Module
docs.text:
Use a submodule when the application is intentionally scoped to one modality:

TextImageAudio 
from instructions import text

system_instruction = text.EXPERT_PROGRAMMER

from instructions import image

system_instruction = image.IMAGE_ANALYZER

from instructions import audio

system_instruction = audio.VERBATIM_TRANSCRIBER

docs.title: Dynamic Lookup
docs.text:
When the instruction name comes from a configuration file, database, UI control, or runtime request, use get() instead of indexing module globals directly:

from instructions import get

instruction_name = 'DATA_SCIENTIST'
system_instruction = get( instruction_name )

An unknown name raises KeyError:

from instructions import get

try:
    system_instruction = get( 'NOT_A_GURO_PROMPT' )
except KeyError as ex:
    print( ex )

docs.title: Discover Available Instructions
docs.text:
from instructions import names

for instruction_name in names( ):
    print( instruction_name )

For a modality-specific list:

from instructions import image

for instruction_name in image.names( ):
    print( instruction_name )

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text:
• Read Choosing the Right Module before wiring Guro into a multi-modal application.
  • Use Discovery & Dynamic Lookup for menus, selectors, or configuration-driven prompts.
  • See Integrating with LLM APIs for provider-neutral usage patterns.
  • Browse the full prompt catalog when selecting a prompt by capability.

docs.title: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'instructions'
docs.text: Run the example from the repository root or install/package the project so the directory containing instructions/ is on sys.path.

docs.title: KeyError from get()
docs.text:
get() accepts only names declared in the relevant module's __all__.

from instructions import names

print( 'IMAGE_ANALYZER' in names( ) )

If you are using a modality-specific module, confirm the prompt belongs to that modality:

from instructions import image

print( 'IMAGE_ANALYZER' in image.names( ) )

docs.title: MkDocs cannot import instructions
docs.text: Build the site from the repository root. The mkdocstrings handler is configured with paths: [.], so changing the working directory can prevent module discovery.

docs.title: Mermaid diagrams appear as code blocks
docs.text:
Confirm both of these are present in mkdocs.yml:

  • the Mermaid custom fence under pymdownx.superfences;
  • the Mermaid JavaScript asset before javascripts/extra.js.

docs.title: Search or table filters do not work after navigation
docs.text: Guro uses MkDocs Material instant navigation. extra.js subscribes to the Material document$ lifecycle and reinitializes enhancements after page swaps. If custom scripts replace this behavior, preserve that subscription.

docs.title: Documentation build fails in strict mode
docs.text:
Run:

mkdocs build --strict -v

Check the first reported navigation, Markdown, plugin, or import failure rather than disabling strict mode. Strict mode is intentional because stale documentation is a functional defect for a catalog-driven library.

docs.title: User Guide
docs.text: Guro exposes instruction prompts as plain Python strings, but the catalog is large enough that how you select and import a prompt matters. This guide focuses on production usage patterns rather than merely listing constants.

docs.title: Choose an Access Pattern
docs.text: Scenario Recommended Pattern One known prompt Import the constant directly from its modality module. Several prompts from one modality Import text, image, or audio and use module attributes. User-selectable prompt Populate the UI with names() and resolve the selection with get(). Configuration-driven prompt Store the uppercase public name and call get() at runtime. Cross-modality application Use the package-level instructions compatibility surface. Need every (name, value) pair Use items() rather than inspecting globals().

docs.text:
flowchart LR
    A[Define task] --> B{Modality?}
    B -->|Text| C[text.py]
    B -->|Image| D[image.py]
    B -->|Audio| E[audio.py]
    C --> F[Select constant]
    D --> F
    E --> F
    F --> G[Pass string to provider/workflow]
    G --> H[Validate result]

docs.title: API Reference
docs.text:
Guro's Python API is deliberately small. The catalog itself consists of constants; four helper functions provide discovery and runtime lookup at package and submodule scope.

API Description names() Returns exported names in declaration order. values() Returns prompt strings in declaration order. items() Returns (name, value) pairs in declaration order. get(name) Returns a validated public prompt by name or raises KeyError.

Use the package-level API for the complete catalog and the module-level API when the application is modality-specific.

docs.title: Development
docs.text: The instruction package is data-heavy but contract-sensitive. Most regressions come from one of four sources: incorrect category routing, a missing export, a duplicate export, or accidental modification of prompt text.

docs.title: Development Invariants
docs.text:
• Every exported prompt is a str.
  • Every package-level export exists.
  • Each prompt belongs to exactly one modality module.
  • Submodule export sets are disjoint.
  • Their union equals the package-level catalog.
  • Prompt text is preserved unless a prompt edit is intentional.
  • New categories require an explicit routing decision.

Read Adding or Updating Prompts before changing the catalog.

docs.title: Adding or Updating Prompts
docs.text: Use the prompt catalog as the source of category metadata and preserve prompt Markdown exactly when transferring content into a Python constant.

docs.title: Add a Prompt
docs.text:
1. Add or update the prompt record in the catalog.
  2. Confirm the Caption, Category, and Text fields.
  3. Convert the caption to the approved uppercase constant name.
  4. Route the prompt according to its category.
  5. Add the constant to the owning module's __all__.
  6. Add the name to package-level instructions.__all__.
  7. Run the validation suite described in Testing & Validation.
  8. Update the catalog documentation if category structure changes.

docs.title: Preserve Markdown Structure
docs.text:
Prompt text is executable configuration data. Do not flatten Markdown headings or bullets during generation.

Correct:

EXAMPLE = f'''## Role

- First responsibility.
- Second responsibility.

## Instructions

- First instruction.
'''

Incorrect:

## Role- First responsibility.- Second responsibility.## Instructions- First instruction.

docs.title: Naming
docs.text:
• Use uppercase snake case.
  • Preserve intentional compatibility names already exposed publicly.
  • Do not silently rename a public constant without providing a migration strategy.
  • Numeric terms such as 3D should remain semantically intact when that is the established public name.

docs.title: Category Routing
docs.text: Category routing determines module ownership. It is not a fuzzy classification step during runtime; it is a maintenance rule applied when the catalog is generated or updated.

docs.title: Routing Table
docs.text: Categories Module Research / Academic; Prompt Engineering; Writing / Administrative; Compliance / Legal / Budget; Business / Finance / Marketing; Software Engineering; Software Engineer; Data Analytics & Governance; Instruction/ Training / Planning text.py Image Generation; Image Analysis; Image Editing image.py Translation API; Transcription API; Speech API audio.py

docs.title: New Category Checklist
docs.text:
When introducing a new category:

  1. decide its owning modality explicitly;
  2. update the routing table in generation tooling;
  3. regenerate affected modules;
  4. confirm no prompt became uncategorized;
  5. confirm no prompt is exported by two modality modules;
  6. update this documentation and the catalog page.

docs.title: Testing & Validation
docs.text: A successful import is necessary but not sufficient. Validate both Python structure and catalog integrity.

docs.title: Compile Test
docs.text:
python -m py_compile instructions\__init__.py
python -m py_compile instructions   ext.py
python -m py_compile instructions\image.py
python -m py_compile instructionsudio.py

docs.title: API Integrity Test
docs.text:
from instructions import audio, image, text
import instructions

assert len( instructions.__all__ ) == 252
assert len( text.__all__ ) == 172
assert len( image.__all__ ) == 45
assert len( audio.__all__ ) == 35

text_names = set( text.__all__ )
image_names = set( image.__all__ )
audio_names = set( audio.__all__ )

assert text_names.isdisjoint( image_names )
assert text_names.isdisjoint( audio_names )
assert image_names.isdisjoint( audio_names )
assert text_names | image_names | audio_names == set( instructions.__all__ )

for name in instructions.__all__:
    assert isinstance( instructions.get( name ), str )

docs.title: Markdown Preservation Test
docs.text: When regenerating from the catalog, compare the resulting runtime string with the source Text value after only the line-ending normalization explicitly allowed by the generation process.

docs.title: Documentation Build
docs.text:
python -m pip install -r requirements-docs.txt
mkdocs build --strict

A strict build should complete without broken navigation references, malformed configuration, or mkdocstrings import failures.

docs.title: Discovery & Dynamic Lookup
docs.text: The helper API exists so callers do not need to introspect module globals or maintain a second list of prompt names.

docs.title: names()
docs.text:
Use names() to build selectors and enumerate the supported public surface.

from instructions import names

available = names( )

docs.title: get()
docs.text:
Resolve a validated public name at runtime:

docs.title: Keep Provider Configuration Outside Guro
docs.text:
Guro should not own:

  • API keys or credentials.
  • Model IDs.
  • Retry/backoff policy.
  • Provider-specific file uploads.
  • Streaming state.
  • Token accounting.
  • Image dimensions or audio codec configuration.

This separation keeps the catalog reusable across SDKs and prevents provider behavior from leaking into prompt definitions.

docs.title: Choosing the Right Module
docs.text:
Use the prompt category—not merely the wording of a prompt name—to select the owning module.

Need Module Research, writing, finance, engineering, analytics, governance, training, planning text.py Generate, analyze, or edit images image.py Translate, transcribe, narrate, or synthesize speech audio.py

docs.title: Decision Tree
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A[Start] --> B{Primary input/output modality}
    B -->|Textual reasoning or content| T[text.py]
    B -->|Visual content| I[image.py]
    B -->|Translation / transcript / speech| AU[audio.py]
    T --> U[Use unified package if app spans modalities]
    I --> U
    AU --> U

docs.title: Cross-Modality Applications
docs.text:
A single application can legitimately use all three modules. For example, a document workflow might:

  1. use an image-analysis prompt to interpret a scanned figure;
  2. use a text prompt to summarize the surrounding document; and
  3. use a speech prompt to narrate the resulting summary.

In that case, importing the package-level compatibility surface is appropriate.

docs.title: Recommended Uses
docs.text:
• System/developer instructions for LLM conversations.
  • Reusable role definitions for internal AI tools.
  • Prompt selection controls in Streamlit, Dash, Flask, or desktop applications.
  • Configuration-driven agent behavior.
  • Evaluation and regression testing of prompt libraries.

Prefer module ownership over name guessing

A prompt beginning with DATA_ is usually text-oriented, but module ownership is authoritative. Use the catalog or the module's names() result instead of inferring modality from the constant name.
